lessons.title: Problem decomposition
lessons.objective: Build competition-ready understanding of problem decomposition and apply it accurately to unfamiliar challenges.
lessons.core_teaching_content: Coding challenges are solved by decomposing requirements, choosing data representations, writing precise control flow and testing edge cases. Variables hold values, conditions branch execution, loops repeat work, and functions isolate reusable logic. Focus specifically on problem decomposition. Identify the core concepts, common misconceptions, evidence or procedure required, and the verification step that protects against error. Move from recognition to application: identify what the task tests, choose an appropriate method, execute it carefully, and check the result against the original requirements. Keep an error log that describes the underlying reasoning failure.
examples: A National Coding Challenge task on problem decomposition should begin by identifying the defining clue or requirement before selecting the method.
Create a new problem decomposition scenario with one plausible distractor and explain why the preferred answer or solution satisfies the requirements.
lessons.practical_activity: Complete a focused National Coding Challenge activity on problem decomposition using a worked problem, diagram, table, passage, code trace or comparison as appropriate.
lessons.guided_practice: Work through three scaffolded tasks on problem decomposition: model the first, prompt the second, and require an independent solution to the third with explicit justification.
independent_practice: Solve three unfamiliar problem decomposition questions or tasks without viewing solutions.
Create and complete one new challenge using the lesson principle.
Analyse one error and write the rule or strategy that would prevent it next time.
lessons.assessment_checkpoint: Complete an eight-item National Coding Challenge checkpoint on problem decomposition; target at least six correct and justify uncertain responses.
lessons.student_task: Produce one finished National Coding Challenge task demonstrating problem decomposition and document the reasoning, evidence or performance criteria used.
lessons.tutor_guidance: Coach for precise terminology, evidence and independent verification. Ask learners to explain the method before confirming the answer. Suitable for self-learning.
lessons.reflection_completion: Record one strength, one recurring error and one measurable action for improving problem decomposition.
lessons.daily_flow: Learn → Worked Example → Guided Challenge → Independent Practice → Check → Reflect
